cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: every goose gets one vote. Gerald has drafted it in mud. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Pass it.
right.reaction: Passed. Turnout tomorrow: four hundred geese. Gerald voted forty times.

left.label: No. Scrap it.
left.reaction: Scrapped. Gerald has eaten the scrap. And the bin.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: lunch lasts until Doug finishes his sandwich. Doug eats very slowly. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Long lunches.
right.reaction: Lunch is two hours now. Productivity is down. Doug is radiant.

left.label: No. Thirty minutes.
left.reaction: Doug is eating faster. He's not enjoying it. He wants that noted.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: every pothole must be named before it's filled. Kevin chairs the naming committee. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Name them.
right.reaction: Tomorrow's potholes: Kevin II, Kevina and Steve. Nobody can bear to fill them.

left.label: No. Just fill them.
left.reaction: Filled, unnamed. Kevin watched. Relieved or jealous, it's hard to say.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: shops shut at eight so the town gets some sleep. Chad calls it 'a crime against shops'. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Early nights.
right.reaction: The town slept. Chad didn't. He stood outside his shop all night, open.

left.label: No. Open late.
left.reaction: Shops open till three. Randy has bought nine torches. Nobody knows why.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: the Bugle may only print good news on Mondays. Marge has fainted. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Good news only.
right.reaction: Monday's headline: 'NICE WEATHER, PROBABLY'. Marge is in recovery.

left.label: No. Print it all.
left.reaction: Marge has revived. She's printing the news that you nearly passed it.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: Randy may not enter the treasury alone. Randy says he'll be 'with his coat'. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Escorted only.
right.reaction: Randy stayed out. His cousins did not. Doug is counting the cousins.

left.label: No. Trust Randy.
left.reaction: Randy is touched. The treasury is lighter. Randy is heavier.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: every council meeting ends with a song. Coach has written it. It's eleven minutes. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Sing it.
right.reaction: Tomorrow's meeting was all song. Two motions passed in harmony.

left.label: No. Just meet.
left.reaction: Coach is singing it anyway. In the corridor. Alone. Beautifully.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: no more than forty traffic cones on any one street. Clive has no comment. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Forty max.
right.reaction: By morning, exactly forty cones on every street. Clive counted.

left.label: No. Unlimited cones.
left.reaction: Fifty cones on Main Street by dawn. Clive's people have mobilised.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: a fine for loud honking after midnight. Gerald has already hired Mr Whiskers. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Fine the honk.
right.reaction: The first fine went to Gerald. He paid in bread. Then honked about it.

left.label: No. Honk freely.
left.reaction: Gerald honked his thanks. All night. Under your window.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: one free sandwich a week for every resident. Doug did the maths and went very pale. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Free sandwiches.
right.reaction: The happiest town in the county. Doug is eating his feelings. In sandwich form.

left.label: No. Buy your own.
left.reaction: Bev has started a sandwich black market. It's very well run.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: a pothole tax on big businesses. Chad says Kevin is not his fault. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Tax them.
right.reaction: Chad paid. Under protest. In coins. He threw them into Kevin.

left.label: No. Leave Chad be.
left.reaction: Chad has thanked you with a plaque. It's for himself.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: Wendy the ghost gets a vote. She's been asking since 1890. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Wendy votes.
right.reaction: Wendy voted. Her ballot floated into the box on its own. A first.

left.label: No. Not yet.
left.reaction: Wendy is disappointed. The lights flickered all night. Pointedly.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: the library stays open all night. Linda would like to know who'll run it. It's Linda. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Open all night.
right.reaction: Four night readers and an owl. Linda has never been happier. Or more tired.

left.label: No. Normal hours.
left.reaction: Linda has gone home. Hoot is reading through the window.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: all billboards must tell the truth. Chad's says 'CHAD: PROBABLY FINE'. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Truth only.
right.reaction: Chad's new billboard: 'CHAD: OKAY'. Sales are down. Honesty is up.

left.label: No. Advertise freely.
left.reaction: Chad's billboard now says 'CHAD: BEST MAYOR'. He isn't mayor.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: Barb's helicopter may not land on the school. Barb says it's 'the only flat bit'. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Not the school.
right.reaction: Barb landed on the library instead. Linda shushed the helicopter.

left.label: No. It's flat.
left.reaction: Helicopter on the school roof by nine. Lessons are loud. Very loud.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: every new building must include a pond. Gerald wrote it. In bread. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Ponds for all.
right.reaction: The new bakery has a pond. The bread is damp. The geese are delighted.

left.label: No. Dry buildings.
left.reaction: Gerald has dug a pond in protest. In your car park. It's lovely.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: the mayor's salary is paid in crisps. Gary has offered to supply them. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Pay me in crisps.
right.reaction: The treasury saves a fortune. The Bugle calls you 'Mayor Crisps'.

left.label: No. Pay me in money.
left.reaction: Gary is hurt. He's dispensed a single sad crisp. For you.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: nobody may be mayor of Bad Town and also a traffic cone. Clive's lawyer is a smaller cone. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. No cone mayors.
right.reaction: Passed. Clive has moved one inch to the left. It feels like a threat.

left.label: No. Cones welcome.
left.reaction: Clive has a campaign office again. It's the same window.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: forecasts must be wrong on purpose, so Steve can be right. Steve is in tears. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Help Steve.
right.reaction: Steve forecast rain to get sun. It rained. He's devastated. And right.

left.label: No. Let Steve be Steve.
left.reaction: Steve forecast sun. It snowed. Order is restored.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: once a week, the whole town says thank you to Doug. Doug drafted it. He's very nervous. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. Thank Doug.
right.reaction: Four thousand thank-yous. Doug cried at every one. It took all day.

left.label: No. He knows.
left.reaction: Doug says it's fine. It is not fine. He's in the stationery cupboard.

cards.text: Draft law for tomorrow: the town motto changes from 'Well, We Tried' to 'Well, We'll Try'. Bev calls it ambitious. Pass it?

right.label: Yes. We'll try.
right.reaction: New signs by morning. Several people have actually tried. It was unsettling.

left.label: No. We tried.
left.reaction: The old motto stays. Everyone is quietly relieved.

cards.text: Boss. Project for tomorrow: I repaint every bin in town. Gold. 'Premium bins'. Approve it?

right.label: Yes. Gold bins.
right.reaction: Every bin is gold by morning. People put rubbish in very carefully. Proudly.

left.label: No. Normal bins.
left.reaction: Randy has painted one bin gold anyway. He lives in it now.

cards.text: Mayor. Project for tomorrow: fix the leak in the treasury roof. Coins drip into the river. The ducks have noticed. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Fix the leak.
right.reaction: Fixed. The ducks are furious. They'd been saving up.

left.label: No. Leave it.
left.reaction: The ducks are now the richest residents of Bad Town.

cards.text: Big Carl. Project for tomorrow: I dig a pool. Myself. With a spoon. I've started. Can I carry on?

right.label: Yes. Dig, Carl.
right.reaction: He's dug a hole the size of a bath. He's guarding it. It's his best day.

left.label: No. Put the spoon down.
left.reaction: He's put it down. He's looking at it. Longingly.

cards.text: Mayor, project for tomorrow: solar panels on City Hall. Experimental. They run on moonlight. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Moon power.
right.reaction: They work. Only at night. City Hall is very bright at 3am.

left.label: No. Normal power.
left.reaction: Nora has installed them on her own shed. It glows. Gerald visits.

cards.text: The PTA would like to plant a hundred trees tomorrow. Toby has offered to supervise. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Plant them.
right.reaction: A hundred new trees. Toby rustled with pride. They're all named after him.

left.label: No. Not this year.
left.reaction: Pam has planted one tree. In your office. Toby is watching through the window.

cards.text: Mayor. Project for tomorrow: a shopping centre. On the roundabout. Reginald is the roundabout. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Build it.
right.reaction: Built round Reginald. He's the centrepiece. He hasn't noticed.

left.label: No. Leave Reginald.
left.reaction: Chad has built a smaller one. On the next roundabout. Also Reginald, later.

cards.text: Mayor, project for tomorrow: a 'Meet the Mayor' day. You, in a booth, all day, answering anything. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Ask me anything.
right.reaction: Four hundred questions. Two hundred were about Kevin. You did your best.

left.label: No booth.
left.reaction: Marge put a cardboard cut-out of you in the booth. It's doing well.

cards.text: Mayor. Project for tomorrow: a police open day. Anyone can try the helicopter. Anyone. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Open day.
right.reaction: Bev flew the helicopter. Twice round the clock tower. Upside down once.

left.label: No. Not anyone.
left.reaction: Barb has opened the helicopter to Biscuit only. He's a natural.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald's plans for tomorrow: a bridge for geese. It goes nowhere. It's very beautiful.) Approve?

right.label: Yes. Build the bridge.
right.reaction: The bridge to nowhere is finished. The geese stand on it at sunset. It's moving.

left.label: No bridge.
left.reaction: Gerald has built it anyway. Out of bread. It lasted until lunch.

cards.text: Mayor, project for tomorrow: a book club for the whole town. The first book is the phone book. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Book club.
right.reaction: Four hundred members. Nobody finished. Everyone has opinions about the Smiths.

left.label: No. Read alone.
left.reaction: Linda has started the book club anyway. It's her and Hoot. Hoot likes the Ps.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. Project for tomorrow: two-beak delivery. Me and a seagull. It's Lorraine. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Two beaks.
right.reaction: Twice as fast. Half the post arrived. The other half was eaten. Lorraine.

left.label: No. One beak.
left.reaction: Lorraine is delivering on her own. Only chips. Only to herself.

cards.text: Mayor, project for tomorrow: driving lessons for everyone. On my scooter. Top speed only. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Teach them.
right.reaction: Forty pupils. All passed. All very shaken. One is still going.

left.label: No lessons.
left.reaction: Bev is giving lessons anyway. To Gerald. He's terrifying on a scooter.

cards.text: Mayor. Project for tomorrow: my second restaurant. Tyres only. No food. A tyre restaurant. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Open it.
right.reaction: Fully booked. Nobody ate. Everyone left with a tyre. Five stars.

left.label: No. One is enough.
left.reaction: Sal is serving tyres at the first restaurant now. Same thing, really.

cards.text: Mayor! Project for tomorrow: a town fun run! Everyone! Even Reginald! He started yesterday! Approve?

right.label: Yes. Everyone runs.
right.reaction: Everyone ran. Shops shut. Reginald is still on mile one. Cheering section intact.

left.label: No running.
left.reaction: Coach is running round the town alone. Shouting 'GOOD PACE' at himself.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot proposes moving tomorrow's school day to tonight. The children are asleep. He'd wake them.) Approve?

right.label: Yes. Night school.
right.reaction: The children were very confused. They learned owls. All of them.

left.label: No. Let them sleep.
left.reaction: Hoot taught the lesson anyway. To an empty classroom. It went well.

cards.text: Mayor! Project for tomorrow: the town app! It's a button. It says 'Bad Town'. That's all it does. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Launch it.
right.reaction: Four thousand downloads. Everyone pressed the button. Nothing happened. Five stars.

left.label: No app.
left.reaction: Brayden has launched it anyway. Just on his phone. He presses it a lot.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. Can tomorrow be volcano day? I built a volcano in the park. It's mostly vinegar. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Volcano day.
right.reaction: It erupted at noon. Everything smells of vinegar. Timmy is a hero.

left.label: No volcanoes.
left.reaction: Timmy erupted it anyway. In his bedroom. His mum has written to you.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. Project for tomorrow: a Squirrel Bank branch inside City Hall. Very convenient. For me. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Open a branch.
right.reaction: Interest rates are terrible. The tellers are squirrels. Doug has opened an account.

left.label: No branch.
left.reaction: Mr Nutkins has opened one in the tree outside. It looks in through your window.

cards.text: Wooo. Project for tomorrow: haunted tours of City Hall for schools. Gently haunted. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Gentle haunting.
right.reaction: The children loved it. Wendy said 'boo' very softly. One child said it back.

left.label: No tours.
left.reaction: Wendy is giving the tour anyway. To the cleaners. They're unbothered.

cards.text: Stormy Steve. Project for tomorrow: I deliver the forecast in person. On every doorstep. It'll take all day. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Door to door.
right.reaction: He told four hundred people it would rain. It was sunny. They were charmed.

left.label: No. Use the radio.
left.reaction: Radio forecast: rain. It rained. Steve doesn't know how to feel.

cards.text: (A note under the vault door reads TOMORROW: CHEESE FAIR. Nobody wrote it. The cheese seems keen.) Approve the fair?

right.label: Yes. Cheese fair.
right.reaction: Very popular. The cheese did not move. The cheese did not need to.

left.label: No fair.
left.reaction: The note has been replaced: TOMORROW: CHEESE FAIR ANYWAY.

cards.text: (It's late. Trevor the moth is at your window. He'd like to come in and sit on your lamp. Just for tonight.) Let him in?

right.label: Yes. Come in, Trevor.
right.reaction: He sat on the lamp until dawn. He said it was the best night of his life.

left.label: No. Goodnight, Trevor.
left.reaction: He's on the streetlight outside. Looking in. Lovingly. All night.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull lands on your desk at midnight. She has a chip. She'd like to talk business.) Hear her out?

right.label: Yes. Talk business.
right.reaction: She's offered to run the seafront. For chips. You've agreed to nothing. Somehow.

left.label: No. Out.
left.reaction: She left the chip. It's a business card, apparently.

cards.text: Boss. Can't sleep. Can we talk? It's about the bins. It's always about the bins. Five minutes?

right.label: Yes. Five minutes.
right.reaction: It was forty minutes. You know a great deal about bins now. You feel closer.

left.label: No. Bed, Randy.
left.reaction: He's gone to bed. In a bin. He's talking to it instead.

cards.text: Wooo. Mayor. It's midnight. My favourite time. Fancy a cup of tea? I can't drink it. I just like making it.

right.label: Yes. Tea with Wendy.
right.reaction: Lovely tea. She told you about 1890. It sounded awful. She misses it.

left.label: No thanks.
left.reaction: She made it anyway. It's on your desk. Steaming. Forever.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot is awake. Of course he is. He'd like to discuss the school budget. Now. In the dark.) Discuss?

right.label: Yes. Discuss.
right.reaction: You agreed a budget at 3am. Mostly for mice. You're not sure how.

left.label: No. Office hours.
left.reaction: He's left a note. It says 'who'. That's the whole note.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald is outside City Hall at 1am. He'd like to come in. He's brought eleven friends.) Let them in?

right.label: Yes. Come in.
right.reaction: Twelve geese in the council chamber. They've chosen their seats. Permanently.

left.label: No. Closed.
left.reaction: They honked until dawn. In shifts. Very organised.

cards.text: (At 2am, you hear humming from the vault. It's quite a nice tune. It's getting louder.) Hum along?

right.label: Yes. Hum along.
right.reaction: You hummed a duet with the cheese. It was beautiful. You'll never tell anyone.

left.label: No. Earplugs.
left.reaction: The humming stopped the moment you put them in. It knows.

cards.text: (Councillor Pebbles is in your office at midnight. He's eating tomorrow's agenda. Slowly. Making eye contact.) Stop him?

right.label: Yes. Stop him.
right.reaction: You saved half the agenda. The other half is Pebbles now.

left.label: No. Let him eat.
left.reaction: Tomorrow's meeting has no agenda. It's the best meeting in months.

cards.text: (Toby the oak tree is tapping on your window with a branch. He can't sleep either. He'd like company.) Keep him company?

right.label: Yes. Sit with Toby.
right.reaction: You sat under Toby until sunrise. A squirrel brought you a nut. It was nice.

left.label: No. Curtains.
left.reaction: He's tapping more quietly now. Sadly. In morse code. It says 'oh'.

cards.text: (Gary the vending machine is the only light on the high street. He's dispensed you a hot chocolate. Unasked.) Drink it?

right.label: Yes. Drink it.
right.reaction: It was 1987 hot chocolate. It was perfect. Gary hummed with joy.

left.label: No thanks.
left.reaction: Gary has dispensed a sad biscuit. As an apology. For nothing.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. Night post. I have a letter addressed to 'The Mayor, Tomorrow'. Shall I give it to you now?

right.label: Yes. Open it now.
right.reaction: It's from you. Tomorrow's you. It says 'don't'. It doesn't say what.

left.label: No. Tomorrow.
left.reaction: He'll deliver it tomorrow. He's holding it in his beak. He can't sleep either.

cards.text: (Kevin the pothole looks different at night. Deeper. Thoughtful. People have left candles in him.) Leave the candles?

right.label: Yes. Leave them.
right.reaction: Kevin glowed all night. Someone wrote a song about it. It's mostly the word 'Kevin'.

left.label: No. Fire risk.
left.reaction: Barb blew them out. One at a time. She said sorry to Kevin each time.

cards.text: (Inspector Biscuit is on night patrol. He has arrested a shadow. It's yours.) Turn yourself in?

right.label: Yes. Fair cop.
right.reaction: You spent ten minutes in a cell. Biscuit gave you a biscuit. Justice was done.

left.label: No. Run.
left.reaction: You ran. Biscuit chased your shadow round the square. He's still chasing it.

cards.text: (Marcel the mime is outside your window, miming 'goodnight'. It's taking a very long time.) Mime it back?

right.label: Yes. Mime goodnight.
right.reaction: You mimed goodnight. He mimed 'you're welcome'. It's been an hour.

left.label: No. Close the curtains.
left.reaction: He's mimed a window. Inside your curtains. Somehow.

cards.text: Boss. I found the big red button that turns off every streetlight. The label says DO NOT PRESS AT NIGHT. It's night. Press it?

right.label: Yes. Press it.
right.reaction: Click. Very dark. Very quiet. Then a lot of honking.

left.label: No. Leave it.
left.reaction: You left it. Randy pressed it once. Just to check. You turned it back on.

cards.text: Mayor, the night bus driver has fallen asleep at the wheel. Doug says if nobody takes over, the bus goes into the river. Take the wheel?

right.label: Yes. Take the wheel.
right.reaction: You drove the night bus home. Four passengers. All asleep. All safe.

left.label: No. Someone else will.
left.reaction: Nobody else did.

cards.text: Mayor, my sleep machine works! Warning on the side: ANYONE WHO PRESSES GO SLEEPS FOR A WEEK. Want to try it?

right.label: Yes. Press GO.
right.reaction: You pressed GO. Mmm.

left.label: No thanks.
left.reaction: Nora tested it on Gerald. Blissful week. For everyone.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald offers you his midnight bread. The bag reads: PROPERTY OF 400 GEESE. TOUCH AND SEE.) Take a slice?

right.label: Yes. Just one slice.
right.reaction: You took a slice. Four hundred heads turned.

left.label: No thank you.
left.reaction: Gerald looked relieved. So did the four hundred geese behind him.

cards.text: Wooo. The clock tower stairs are rotten. The sign says DO NOT CLIMB. I'd like to show you the view from the top. Climb?

right.label: Yes. Climb it.
right.reaction: Lovely view. For about four steps.

left.label: No. Describe it.
left.reaction: Wendy floated up and described it. It sounded lovely. Mostly roofs.

cards.text: Mayor. The vault must be locked before midnight or the cheese gets out. That's the rule. It's 11:59. Lock it?

right.label: Yes. Lock it now.
right.reaction: Locked at 11:59 and 50 seconds. Something inside sighed. You slept well.

left.label: No. It'll keep.
left.reaction: It did not keep.

cards.text: Mayor! Late-night deal. Sign this napkin and the town is mine 'for one night only'. Small print: forever. Sign?

right.label: Yes. One night only.
right.reaction: You signed. Chad read the small print aloud. Slowly. Twice.

left.label: No. I read the small print.
left.reaction: Chad has eaten the napkin. He says it was 'a joke napkin'.

cards.text: (Mr Whiskers Esq. is on your desk at midnight. He has knocked your pen to the floor. He's eyeing the stapler.) Move the stapler?

right.label: Yes. Save the stapler.
right.reaction: You saved the stapler. He knocked over your tea instead. He held eye contact throughout.

left.label: No. Let fate decide.
left.reaction: The stapler is on the floor. So is the lamp. Mr Whiskers is asleep. Case closed.

cards.text: (Reginald the tortoise has reached your door. He set off at lunchtime. He'd like to say hello.) Say hello back?

right.label: Yes. Hello, Reginald.
right.reaction: He's started back home, delighted. He'll be there by Thursday.

left.label: No. It's very late.
left.reaction: He's turned round. Slowly. It'll be the slowest sulk in history.

cards.text: (A traffic cone has appeared outside your bedroom window. It's Clive. Nobody saw him arrive. Nobody ever does.) Move him?

right.label: Yes. Move Clive.
right.reaction: You moved him to the kerb. In the morning he was back. Closer.

left.label: No. Leave him be.
left.reaction: The Bugle has a photo: 'MAYOR AND CONE: THE TRUTH'. There is no truth. It's a cone.

cards.text: (Mr Nutkins is on your windowsill with a tiny briefcase. He'd like to discuss your overdraft. At the Squirrel Bank.) Let him in?

right.label: Yes. Discuss it.
right.reaction: You now owe four acorns. With interest. He's very pleased.

left.label: No. Office hours.
left.reaction: He's left a statement on the sill. It's a leaf. You're in the red.

cards.text: Big Carl. Can't sleep. I'm guarding the town. From the night. Can I guard it from your office? It's warmer.

right.label: Yes. Guard away.
right.reaction: Carl guarded your office all night. Nothing got in. Not even morning, almost.

left.label: No. Go home, Carl.
left.reaction: He's guarding your doorstep. Shivering. Heroically.

cards.text: (Inspector Biscuit is at your door with a sausage. Evidence, apparently. He'd like you to hold it while he thinks.) Hold it?

right.label: Yes. Hold the evidence.
right.reaction: He thought for an hour. Then ate the evidence. Case closed.

left.label: No. Not the sausage.
left.reaction: He's holding it himself. Badly. It's half gone. The investigation continues.

cards.text: Mayor, it's Marge. Late edition. One quick quote for tomorrow's front page? Anything. Anything at all.

right.label: Yes. One quote.
right.reaction: You said 'goodnight'. Tomorrow's headline: 'MAYOR SAYS GOODNIGHT: WHAT DID THEY MEAN?'

left.label: No comment.
left.reaction: Tomorrow's headline: 'NO COMMENT'. Somehow it sold out.

trap:ah_lights.title: Lights Out
trap:ah_lights.text: Every streetlight off at once. The geese took the town by midnight. You are now mayor of the bit under your desk.

trap:ah_bus.title: Last Stop: River
trap:ah_bus.text: The night bus went into the river. Everyone swam out. The bus is a reef now. The ducks charge admission.

trap:ah_sleep.title: Sleeping on the Job
trap:ah_sleep.text: You slept for a week. The town ran itself. It was fine. That's the worst part. It was completely fine.

trap:ah_bread.title: Breadwinner
trap:ah_bread.text: Four hundred geese took the slice back. Then your shoes. Then your office. Gerald is mayor now. He's very good.

trap:ah_tower.title: Down the Clock Tower
trap:ah_tower.text: You made it four steps, then went through all of them. You're fine. The clock now strikes 'ow' on the hour.

trap:ah_cheese.title: The Cheese Is Out
trap:ah_cheese.text: At midnight the vault door creaked. By one it was running the council. By two, it had a fan club. You are in it.

trap:ah_napkin.title: Signed Away
trap:ah_napkin.text: You signed the napkin. Bad Town is now Chadtown, forever. The welcome sign is his face. It winks.
